definitions.meaning: a play by Will Shakespeare, his last solo comedy of storm and shipwreck

explanation.surface: Someone keeps on labouring through a storm.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's late play shares its title with the word for a violent storm, so one name covers both the drama and the gale.

definitions.meaning: Kipling wrote that East and West are a pair that 'never shall meet', using the old word for two

explanation.surface: Kipling is cast as a comic writer of East and West.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic word for a pair appears in Kipling's famous line about East and West, and it is also the pen name of the author of Huckleberry Finn.

clue.text: Writer shows keenness and some merit

parts.note: a blade's keenness is its edge
merit or value is worth

explanation.surface: An author displays sharpness and a fair amount of talent.
explanation.walkthrough: Maria Edgeworth was an Anglo-Irish novelist of the early 1800s.
explanation.definitionFit: Maria Edgeworth was a novelist, author of Castle Rackrent.

clue.text: Cake made up of grain: about a pound

indicators.note: the rearranged grain goes about, or around, the other letters
something made up is put together afresh, so the letters of the grain are rearranged

parts.note: rice is a cereal grain
L is the abbreviation for a pound (librum)

explanation.surface: A bake whose recipe is mostly grain and weighs about a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made up of' scrambles RICE to ECIR, and 'about' puts L and A inside it: EC(LA)IR.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclair is a long choux-pastry cake filled with cream.

clue.text: Announced as in favour of decimal coinage

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: coinage is the minting of something new, so the letters of decimal are recast

explanation.surface: A remark about supporting a switch to decimal currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coinage' rearranges DECIMAL into CLAIMED, after PRO.
explanation.definitionFit: To proclaim is to announce publicly, so the past tense matches.

clue.text: Port that is knocked back by a god

indicators.note: being knocked back sends the god's name the other way, read from right to left

parts.note: Zeus is the chief Greek god

explanation.surface: A harbour town is driven back by a deity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is knocked back' turns ZEUS round.
explanation.definitionFit: Suez is the Egyptian port at the southern end of the Suez Canal.

definitions.meaning: a boss is a raised knob or ornamental ..., as on a shield

explanation.definitionFit: A stud is both a decorative knob, the sense of boss on a shield or door, and an establishment of breeding horses.

indicators.note: the revolution goes round, enclosing the numeral

parts.note: a revolution is a turn
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An uprising surrounds a single city.
explanation.definitionFit: Turin is a major city of northern Italy.

parts.note: Down is a county of Northern Ireland
to school someone is to train them

explanation.surface: A county's school is given buses.
explanation.walkthrough: A down train runs away from London, the opposite of an up train.
explanation.definitionFit: A down train is a railway service heading away from the capital, a means of travel.

clue.text: Concerning exalted bodies changing rates about two pounds

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go about, around, the pounds
changing the word rates shuffles its letters into a new order

parts.note: L is a pound, so two pounds are two Ls

explanation.surface: Something about lofty personages and fluctuating prices by a couple of pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' makes STEAR from RATES, and 'about' puts LL inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Stellar means relating to stars, the heavenly bodies high above us.

definitions.meaning: an old English gold coin, which would buy things

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a heavenly being and also an old gold coin stamped with St Michael, money that once bought goods.

definitions.meaning: to topple or defeat a ruler
in cricket, a throw past the stumps that lets the batsmen take an extra run or more

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a fielder's throw that misses and lets the batsmen run again gives runs called this.
explanation.definitionFit: To topple a government is to bring it down; in cricket the word is a wild return from a fielder giving extra runs.

definitions.note: the definition names a place found in Derbyshire

parts.note: modern means new
mills are factory buildings

explanation.surface: Recent factories put up in an English county.
explanation.walkthrough: New Mills is a small town in Derbyshire, an English county in the Midlands, once full of cotton mills.
explanation.definitionFit: New Mills is a market town located in the county of Derbyshire.

annotationWithheld.why: Space traveller has tree-top work-out (6): PLANE (tree) + T needs 'tree-top' both as PLANE and as the T from its top, and 'work-out' then has no job; one word doing two jobs

clue.text: Risks coming about in the country

parts.note: an advent is a coming or arrival

indicators.note: the short word for about sits in the country's letters

parts.note: US is the United States, the country
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Dangers arriving in the land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts RE inside US, after ADVENT: ADVENT + U(RE)S.
explanation.definitionFit: Adventures are hazardous undertakings, ventures where something is at stake.

clue.text: Unusual to put it in for a repair

annotationWithheld.why: Unusual to put it in for a repair (4): no parse of 'to put it in for a repair' gives RARE; the scan shows the same words and no fuller print was found
annotationWithheld.clue: Unusual to put it in for a repair

parts.note: a policeman's beat is his round
the head is the chief

explanation.surface: A police officer's patrol leader opposes the king.
explanation.walkthrough: Roundheads were the Parliamentarians who fought Charles I in the English Civil War.
explanation.definitionFit: The Parliamentarian soldiers, so called for their cropped hair, fought the royalists of Charles I.

indicators.note: by speech means as spoken, so the word is matched by its sound

parts.note: to offend against morality is to have sinned

explanation.surface: A region of Pakistan is upset by a remark.
explanation.definitionFit: Sind, also spelt Sindh, is a province in southern Pakistan around Karachi.

clue.text: Articles about a small case of depression in Wicklow

indicators.note: the two articles go about, around, the case

parts.note: A is the indefinite article; two of them give two As
voc. is the short form of the vocative case in grammar

explanation.surface: Newspaper pieces about a little box containing an Irish melancholy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small case' is an abbreviated grammatical case, VOC (vocative). The Vale of Avoca is a valley in County Wicklow, Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vale of Avoca is a valley, a hollow in the land, in County Wicklow.

clue.text: Working on speech about physical education

indicators.note: the speech goes about, around, the school subject

parts.note: an oration is a formal speech

explanation.surface: Someone is busy on a talk about school sports.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts PE inside ORATION. 'Working' fits as in 'the plant is in operation'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in action or functioning is in operation, so 'working' and the noun match in the phrase 'in operation'.

clue.text: His civic honour involves no chain of office

definitions.text: His civic honour involves no chain of office

parts.words: His civic honour involves no chain of office
parts.note: the honour of a town's freedom goes to someone who wears no mayoral chain, and who is unchained, a man at liberty

explanation.definitionFit: A citizen granted the freedom of a city holds that civic honour, and the two words also describe a man who is not in chains.

parts.note: Poe wrote a tale of a doomed family house, and the family name is also that of a man who shows people to their seats

explanation.walkthrough: Poe's story is The Fall of the House of Usher; an usher is also a doorkeeper or attendant.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of the family in Poe's tale is also a word for an attendant at a door or hall.

parts.note: the organs we see with are fringed with lashes, not whipped prophets

explanation.definitionFit: The organs of sight are what see, and they carry lashes.

definitions.meaning: the French form of John, a common name for a man in France
a girl's name, common in Scotland

explanation.definitionFit: The name is masculine in France, like John, but a woman's name in English-speaking countries.

indicators.note: eccentric means odd, out of the ordinary, so the letters of and are rearranged

parts.note: ton is an old word for fashion, as in 'the bon ton'

explanation.surface: A rebel who is also an oddball dresser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' turns AND into DAN, before TON.
explanation.definitionFit: Georges Danton was a leader of the French Revolution.

definitions.note: ditto means the same again, here repeating 'girl' from the clue before

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: mothers of Spain, the same again.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue continues 22-across, so 'ditto' repeats its 'girl'.
explanation.definitionFit: A damsel is a young woman, the same sense as 'girl' in the clue before.

parts.note: 1000 in Roman numerals is M
28 refers to the answer to 28-down, the emperor

explanation.surface: A saying given only as a number.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 1028 as 1000 and 28: M is the Roman numeral for 1000, and 28 stands for the answer to 28-down, OTTO.
explanation.definitionFit: A motto is a short saying or maxim adopted as a guide.

clue.text: Stormy tears about prohibition in Co. Tyrone

definitions.note: the definition names a place found in County Tyrone

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go about, around, the ban
something stormy is turbulent, so the letters of tears are thrown about

parts.note: a ban is a prohibition

explanation.surface: Turbulent weeping over a ban in a Northern Irish county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stormy' makes STRAE from TEARS, and 'about' puts BAN inside: STRA(BAN)E. Strabane is a town in County Tyrone, Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Strabane is a border town located in County Tyrone.

clue.text: Price of course is still a shilling

parts.note: even can mean still, as in 'even more'
s is the abbreviation for a shilling in old British money

explanation.surface: A course's price is still one shilling.
explanation.walkthrough: Evens is betting odds of one to one, a price at the racecourse; s was the abbreviation for the shilling, a coin in Britain before 1971.
explanation.definitionFit: At the racecourse the price, or odds, of even money is quoted as evens.

indicators.note: read up the grid, from bottom to top, the down entry spells the same name

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A ruler surrenders.
explanation.walkthrough: In the grid this down entry reads the same upwards, so the emperor 'gives himself' when read up.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto was the name of several Holy Roman Emperors, such as Otto the Great.

clue.text: He draws out more to get in credit!

parts.note: extra means more

indicators.note: the short word gets in between the letters of the credit abbreviation

explanation.surface: A man pulls out more to get into the black.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get in' puts TO inside CR, after EXTRA: EXTRA + C(TO)R.
explanation.definitionFit: An extractor is someone or something that draws out, like a dentist pulling teeth.

definitions.meaning: a sailor's word meaning to haul up and fasten a sail with a rope

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a moment, as in 'in a ...', and as a nautical verb it means to hoist and lash a sail.

clue.text: Fall in river on way back

indicators.note: back sends the river and road together the other way, read right to left

parts.note: the Po is the river of northern Italy
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: Someone tumbles into a river on the return trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses PO + RD.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop is to fall, as a temperature drops.

clue.text: Members of the L.D.V. and N.F.S. are, literally

definitions.text: Members of the L.D.V. and N.F.S. are, literally

parts.words: Members of the L.D.V. and N.F.S. are, literally
parts.note: the initials of the wartime Local Defence Volunteers and National Fire Service contain no vowels at all

explanation.walkthrough: The L.D.V. (later the Home Guard) and N.F.S. were British wartime services; 'literally' points at their letters, none of which is a vowel.
explanation.definitionFit: Letters other than vowels are the only kind found in those initials, so each letter is one of them.
